metadata.title: TIMSS 2014/15 | SCIENCE | YEAR 9 TRENDS OVER 20 YEARS IN TIMSS

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS sampling and scaling procedures for Year 9 science in TIMSS 2014/15, where means and achievement estimates are adjusted (“weighted”) to reflect the target population rather than the raw sample. It states that TIMSS weighting takes into account school, class, and student level information, and that the overall sampling weight is a product of school, class, and student weights. The report also describes that statistical uncertainty (standard errors) is computed using TIMSS methodology, including a new method for this cycle and recalculation of prior-cycle standard errors. However, the report does not name specific weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight methods, so the exact implementation details for the analysis in this New Zealand report are not fully specified.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive national trends and benchmarking report rather than an empirical student-level predictive modeling study. It reports scaled science achievement and benchmark classifications produced by TIMSS scaling procedures, but it does not describe any plausible-values (PV) workflow or missing-data imputation/deletion strategy for an ML pipeline. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported in the context of this report’s analysis, and the absence is best interpreted as a reporting/level-ofdetail gap for PV/missing-data procedures rather than evidence that no missingness exists.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report analyzes New Zealand Year 9 students from TIMSS 2014/15. Schools were sampled separately for Year 5 and Year 9 with explicit strata based on decile, level of urbanisation, and for Year 9 only, school gender; within each sampled school, two Year 9 classes were sampled and all Year 9 students in those classes were selected. Exclusions in New Zealand included very small schools (fewer than four Year 9 students), special education schools, the Correspondence School, and schools providing more than 50% of instruction in te reo Māori; within schools, special education classes, special needs students, students with insufficient instruction in English, and units providing more than 50% instruction in te reo Māori were excluded. The New Zealand exclusion rate for Year 9 was 3.1%.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2014/15 national report summarizes science achievement for New Zealand Year 9 students and compares results across countries and over time (1994/95 to 2014/15). The assessment is a pencil-and-paper test administered in two timed 45-minute sessions, with multiple-choice and constructed-response items, aligned to a science framework with four content domains (biology, chemistry, physics, Earth science) and three cognitive domains (knowing, applying, reasoning). Achievement is reported on the TIMSS science scale (mean 500, SD 100) with equating across cycles and international science benchmarks at 400/475/550/625. For New Zealand, 8,101 Year 9 students from 137 schools were assessed in Oct–Nov 2014, using TIMSS sampling with school/class/student weighting and standard-error calculations that account for sampling and scaling uncertainty. The report’s conclusions emphasize curriculum-test alignment, domain-specific strengths/weaknesses, and equity patterns (e.g., benchmark proportions and subgroup differences), but it does not implement or evaluate machine-learning models.
